name: Luis Sentis
current_role: Professor of Aerospace Engineering, UT Austin (directs Human Centered Robotics Lab); co-founder & scientific advisor, Apptronik
profile: Catalan-trained roboticist (telecom engineering, UPC) who went to Stanford in 1997, did a PhD on humanoids and worked with Honda and NASA. As a UT Austin professor he led UT's DARPA Robotics Challenge effort with NASA JSC, and in 2016 co-founded Apptronik, spun out of his lab; it builds the Apollo humanoid and is valued ~$5B.
interesting_fact: His whole-body control theory for humanoid robots is described as now used in humanoid robots worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: He went to Stanford in 1997 on a 'la Caixa' Foundation fellowship (he says humanoid robots 'might not exist' without it); the day after arriving he was already discussing robotics with physicist Edward Teller, and he later lived the dot-com boom/bust at a Motorola spin-off.
notes: Academic and approachable; speaks Spanish. University email is the most direct published route.

name: Chris Power
current_role: Founder & CEO, Hadrian (automated precision-parts factories for aerospace & defense, Torrance CA)
profile: Melbourne-born former growth executive (Catch.com, shift-work software startup Ento) who moved to California, began acquiring aerospace supply-chain businesses, and founded Hadrian in late 2020. Hadrian builds highly automated factories making precision metal components for space and defense, backed by a16z, Founders Fund and Lux Capital (~$2B valuation).
interesting_fact: Hadrian's mission is to 'build the planet's most efficient factories to accelerate a free, abundant, spacefaring future'; his pitch: 'If you want something made, we'll make it for you, higher-quality, faster and cheaper.'
deep_cut_fact: He spent five years studying commerce and accounting at Monash University but left in 2013 to pursue business; he was GM of partnerships at CatchOfTheDay and from 2015 head of growth at Airtree-backed Ento before switching to manufacturing.
notes: Outspoken about US reindustrialisation; frequent podcast guest. Personal X handle not verified (web search budget exhausted).

name: Ben Currin
current_role: CEO, Vantaca (HOA / community-association management software, Wilmington NC)
profile: US Naval Academy economics grad who spent nearly a decade as a Navy submarine officer and nuclear engineer, then joined founder Dave Sweyer at Vantaca in late 2017 and became CEO in 2020. He grew the bootstrapped vertical-SaaS company to ~500 management firms and 6M+ homes, bringing in JMI Equity (2022) and Cove Hill (2024); valued ~$1B+.
interesting_fact: Vantaca grew from a few hundred thousand dollars of revenue in 2018 to high-single-digit millions ARR by 2022 entirely bootstrapped, and Currin says it has grown ~10x since.
deep_cut_fact: Before software he trained as a nuclear engineer and led submarine crews on deployments worldwide for nearly a decade.
notes: Has done podcasts (Nathan Latka's The Top, Founderpath, Power of Change) - open to founder-story interviews; 'boring vertical SaaS' angle.

name: Jeff McCoy
profile: Former active-duty Airman (18+ years) and later senior Air Force civilian who worked in SATCOM and network engineering and helped launch Kessel Run, DDS Rogue Squadron, SpaceCAMP and Platform One. Co-founded Defense Unicorns in 2021, where he leads its open-source Zarf, Pepr and Unified Defense Stack; company valued >$1B after a $136M Series B in Jan 2026.
interesting_fact: He led development of Zarf, an airgap software-delivery tool Defense Unicorns donated to the OpenSSF that is now used in aircraft, submarines, space systems and security screening systems.
deep_cut_fact: He started as an enlisted Airman and taught tactical cyber systems as a Community College of the Air Force (CCAF) instructor before rising to senior civilian rank (NH-IV).
